Hi Sofia / Tom,

Thanks again for locking in the architecture deep-dive with our team on Thu 3/12 at 10:00 PT. To make the session as actionable as possible, we've been collecting "parking-lot" questions from our engineers and would love to get any items you want covered ahead of time.

Quick ask: could you share any specific constraints or questions from your infra team (network, E2E auth, data flow, or latency targets) so Dylan can prepare configuration examples and short demos? If you have any docs or a current infra inventory, please attach them.

We pulled a few topics on our side that we'll cover unless you push back:
- Expected QPS and peak concurrent sessions
- VPC peering vs private link options for model payloads
- KV cache behavior for long conversations and costs
- Quantization/precision tradeoffs and any hardware constraints you have

I've attached our suggested agenda and a quick checklist. If you need to reschedule, flag it here and Dev will coordinate alternative times.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Arch deep-dive (Thu 3/12 10:00 PT) — parking-lot questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — the time works for most of the team. A couple of items from our side (internal ops + privacy):

1) Network topology: we'll share a network diagram but to flag: we are likely to require PrivateLink for cross-account model invocations due to our data classification. Can you confirm Redwood has a PrivateLink option and whether session affinity across AZs is preserved?

2) Latency SLO: our internal SLA target is p95 < 350ms for short text completions (<=256 tokens). We want to understand caching behavior for prefix-heavy traffic.

3) Data retention & logs: security needs to confirm what request/response logs are persisted and for how long. We may need to see example audit logs.

Attached is our current infra inventory and a cropped network diagram — apologies for the rough export.

Could Dylan include a short slide showing how Redwood handles PrivateLink/peering and a sample audit log extract?

Cheers,
Sofia
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Analytics
sofia@acmeanalytics.com
[Attachment: network_constraints.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@acmeanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arch deep-dive (Thu 3/12 10:00 PT) — parking-lot questions

Hi Sofia — thanks for the details and the diagram; super helpful. Quick answers to help prep: 

- PrivateLink: yes, we support AWS PrivateLink for hosted integrations plus VPC peering options for Redwood Private deployments. I'll bring a short slide that sketches both patterns and the tradeoffs (TLS termination, cross-account routing, and cost).

- Session affinity / AZ behavior: session affinity is preserved at the connection layer for an invocation; however, for autoscaled Dedicated pools, requests may route to different pods after idle periods. We'll cover best practices for long-lived conversational sessions (KV cache pinning and sticky sessions).

- Latency SLOs: 350ms p95 for <=256 tokens is achievable in many configs — we'll show example profiles and the batching/cache knobs that keep p95 low. If you can share token distribution (short vs long), we can pick the right kernel/quantization combo to demo.

- Audit logs: I'll bring sanitized examples (we'll redact any customer data) showing request IDs, timestamps, model variant, route, and any error fields. 

I'll include two short config snippets: one for PrivateLink + KMS integration, and one for VPC peering with subnet/NACL recommendations. Attaching the snippets here for your review.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[dylan@redwoodinference.com]
[Attachment: private_link_snippet.txt (text/plain)]
